title: Lely's Droom
excerpt: An immersive experience in the Oosterlanderkerk built around rediscovered recordings of Cornelis Lely, made exactly a hundred years earlier.
description:
Lely's Droom is a fifteen minute immersive experience in the Oosterlanderkerk in Oosterland, Wieringen, made for Erfgoedspektakel and shown through May 2025.
It starts from rediscovered sound recordings that Cornelis Lely made in May 1925, exactly a hundred years before the piece was shown. He speaks to whoever is still interested in his dream a century later, appearing in the church as a life size animated figure. Projection and light carry his story: the first plans from 1848, the years of rejection, the flood of January 1916 that killed twenty one people on land and thirty two more at sea, the Zuiderzeewet of 1918, the Amsteldiepdijk built to learn on, the Wieringen boulder clay that finally held, and the Afsluitdijk itself.
Lely died at his desk in January 1929 and never saw the work finished.
> Water is always moving, so waterworks are never finished. That is Lely's own line, and it is the reason the piece is addressed forward rather than back: he is not being commemorated, he is asking what we are doing with the problem now.
> My part was the water and the particles: simulated water moving through the building, and particle work holding the whole show together. A church is already built for stories larger than the room, and flooding it put visitors inside the thing Lely spent his life arguing for, instead of in front of a picture of it.
credits: An installation made with LiGHT-UP Collective for Erfgoedspektakel, Wieringen, 2025. Particle effects and simulated water: Jaco Schilp. Life size animated 3D character of Cornelis Lely, motion graphics, animation, editing and archival research in the Dutch national archives: Tristan Gieler, who also composed and produced the original score. Film: Jokko Voogt. Initiated by BOEi, with Gemeente Hollands Kroon, Culturele Kring Wieringen and the VriendenLoterij.
